notes.notes:

Hoo hoo, deadly little ghostlings! 
Dive into the story of a girl who has returned from the world of the dead with supernatural ghostly powers granted by a God of Death!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1294340/Wonhon_A_Vengeful_Spirit/

[previewyoutube=1cFrtI5ndts;full][/previewyoutube]

It's been a long and tough path, and without your support, we wouldn't have made it. As a result, we'd want to express our gratitude with a simple - [b]THANK YOU[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

A few words from Sean, the developer of [b]Wonhon: A Vengeful Spirit[/b], who alone managed to create something that many people could not do with the team:

[i]“It’s been roughly over 2.5 years since I started developing this game - From December 13th 2018 to July 15th 2021! Developing Wonhon by myself has been a very challenging yet rewarding experience, pushing me to learn all sorts of things about 3D modeling, animation, level design, programming, and many other components that go into creating a game.


Nearly 1000 days of development! I can probably count on one hand the days I took off during all this time, so it really has consumed my life. I remember, the first day of development was entirely spent on creating a low poly version of one of the buildings used in the game. It took some time to figure out, but it looked pretty good by the end of the day. Before starting to develop this game, I didn’t know much about 3d modeling, so just discovering that I could make a low poly approximation of a traditional Korean house in Blender got me excited enough to think I could do this all by myself.
Wonhon was truly a labor of love for me, and I hope that players will feel it as they go through the game. I should also thank Gabsung Lim for the sound design, Alex Park for the story and dialogue in the game, and everyone at Super.com for their support. It wouldn’t have been possible to bring this game to life without their assistance and encouragement. 

If there are any rough spots in the game, please leave your feedback and I’ll do my best to polish it up even after the game is out. I’m excited to send this game out into the world now. Please enjoy the game!”[/i] (с) Sean, [b]Wonhon: A Vengeful Spirit[/b] developer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]


We sincerely hope that our efforts will pay off, and you guys fully enjoy the gameplay of [b]Wonhon: A Vengeful Spirit[/b].
As always, we welcome any and all feedback, so please do let us know what you think about our game.

That’s it, fellow ghostlings. We’re monitoring incoming questions all day'n'night long with our fatigued, red eyes (and that, for once, isn’t a joke).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37518397/152fb1419df0940f7b1106ba900a0a3f6c12c315.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Q&A with Sean: part 3
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37518397/b085d233e9530ea7249c518a93d77e82ac2738d6.png[/img]

Hi, ghosts,


Welcome to the third part of our Q&A posts! In this post, you get to know more about the Wonhon mini-comic books, the hardest game system to make, and the ways of managing your stress during game development.

[b][list]
[*] I find it very interesting to see the scene with assembling crows. Could you tell us more about how you did it? Did you animate each raven separately? How long did it take?
[/list][/b] [i]The crow horde is a big GPU particle system. Each crow is animated using vertex animated textures (using texture blending for multiple animations - idle, gliding, flapping). It took a long time to figure out - I couldn’t rely on the built-in systems for animation, physics, and AI, so it was difficult to try to program all of those things from scratch using compute shaders. [/i]

[b][list]
[*] What made you want to start writing these kinds of comic books?
[/list][/b] [i]The comic books were written by Alex Park. He had ideas on more stories that could be told within that universe, so those turned into the mini comic books.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] What is the most interesting game programming-related story you learned throughout your developing & researching?
[/list][/b] [i]I made a lot of editor tools to speed up my development process, and those were fun to figure out. Unity is really flexible as an engine, so you can do a ton to modify the engine as you wish and make many tools (inspector UI, procedural modeling, fence placement, etc) to make your process more efficient.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] What game system was the hardest one to make?
[/list][/b] [i]Enemy field of view system was tough to figure out. Initially I used CPU raycasting and procedural mesh to build the fan-shaped field of view visualization, but it was very limited. I couldn’t have more than 3 enemies showing their field of view at once, because the frame rate would drop to below 30 fps on a standard gaming PC. This was a huge problem as I wanted every enemy to show their field of view when they were alerted by the player. I looked at how other games handled this problem, and it seems like other games either rely on precomputation using simple level geometry or only show one enemy’s field of view at a time. These solutions didn’t work for Wonhon, so I needed to think of something different. Luckily I’d learned a little bit about GPU programming from making rain and fog particle systems, so I thought I could offload the field of view calculations to the GPU as well.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] Are you planning to continue being a solo dev, or will you be happy to work in a team?
[/list][/b] [i]I guess it depends on what I want to do after this game. I’m not sure yet.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] Can you somehow explain why you chose such a dark and gloomy style for your game?
[/list][/b] [i]I just chose the subject matter and style that appealed to me the most at the start of development. Making a ‘dark’ game wasn’t a conscious choice.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] Why did you choose the Unity engine for your game? 
[/list][/b] [i]I’ve been using Unity for a couple of years, so it was the tool that I was most comfortable with. [/i]

[b][list]
[*] How did you manage your stress? Such an undertaking must've been quite hard.
[/list][/b] [i]Meditation helps with stress management. And I try not to take things too seriously. We’re all here for a limited amount of time, nothing’s worth losing your mind over. Also, I love game development, so even the hard parts were fun problems to solve.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] What would be your best advice for a person who would like to start making their own games?
[/list][/b] [i]Start small and do it everyday![/i]

[b][list]
[*] How long do you think interest in your game will last?
[/list][/b] [i]I think that’s impossible for me to guess. If people get value out of my game, I’d be happy.[/i]

At the moment, our selection of questions is over, so if you want to see more of these posts,  feel free to ask your interesting questions that may be included in a new list in the future.

Thanks for staying with us and simply for reading Sean’s thoughts, we appreciate it!

Take care, friends!

notes.title: Q&A with Sean: Part 2
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37518397/b40b719d826f8ebff6889fd902af96b158091ea2.png[/img]

Hi ghosts,

Welcome to the second part of our Q&A posts! In this post, you get to know more about Sean’s personal preferences, the games from E3 he’s waiting for, and the best and worst parts of being a solo dev.

[h3]The next 10 most interesting questions are next in line:[/h3]

[b][list]
[*] Are there hidden hints, easter eggs, or something like this in the game? How many are there?
[/list][/b] [i]There definitely are hidden secrets in the game. But since they’re secrets, I won’t get into the details too much here.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] What's been your favourite part of development? 
[/list][/b] [i]I really enjoyed graphics programming. Programming stuff for the GPU with compute shaders is really satisfying, especially when it results in some visually striking effects that turn out better than you expected. [/i]

[b][list]
[*] Are there any DLCs already planned for the future?
[/list][/b] [i]Nothing planned for now, but I’ll be supporting the game with fixes and tweaks after the release.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] Was there any desire to tell the story of the main girl char in more detail directly in the game?
[/list][/b] [i]I felt like the main character was an amalgamation of many lost spirits during that time period in Korea, so adding more detail to her story or identity would distract from what I wanted to say in the game. I like her depiction in the game as it is right now.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] If you had to budget and resources to create the perfect game, how would you approach the development?
[/list][/b] [i]I think I would set aside 3 years for prototyping with a small team, maybe around 3 people (preferably all generalists). In 3 years we’d make dozens of prototypes to figure out what we want to do and the best things to put into the final game. And then at the end of the prototyping period, we’d throw out everything we had and put the hard drives in the microwave. Then we’d start fresh on a blank slate with the memory of what we wanted to make, and try to finish the final game in 4 years or so - 2 years for content and 2 years for polishing.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] What are the games from E3 you are looking forward to most?
[/list][/b] [i]I’m really looking forward to playing Fatal Frame 5 port, Elden Ring, and Sable![/i]

[b][list]
[*] What industry trends would you most like to see change? How would you go about changing them?
[/list][/b][i] I’m not sure about trends, but as long as people can continue to make unique games and have the games find their place to the players, I think it’s all good. All I can do is to try to make good games and put them in front of people. [/i] 

[b][list]
[*] What genre of games will be the most popular in the future?
[/list][/b] I think action games and sports games will always be the most popular. I enjoy those games too, so it’s all good.

[b][list]
[*] Any plans on making a game for smartphones?
[/list][/b] [i]I have made smartphone games before, they’re fun. I don’t have plans to go back in the immediate future, but maybe one day. [/i]

[b][list]
[*] What are the best and worst parts about making a game yourself?
[/list][/b] [i]The best thing is that you can very quickly turn your ideas into reality when you can handle every part of the pipeline. The worst thing is that there’s no one else to blame when things go wrong :)[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37518397/cefa90a70a131ae428222bad0dd57b30f9d4f989.jpg[/img]

We genuinely hope that you were interested in reading the post! See you in the next part, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Q&A with Sean: Part 1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37518397/e55cddf2ab6a62da0ee206910f4ca7c0950ba2f1.png[/img]

Hello, ghosts,

Many of you are interested in various questions regarding the game, development, and our talented solo dev Sean and his accomplished path! That's why we decided to collect the best questions for Sean, the answers to which we will post for you!

[h3]Here is the list of the first 10 questions:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Have you made this masterpiece game completely on your own? [/b]
[/list] [i]I had some help from my friends - Gab Lim on music, Alex Park on story, and the publisher Super.com on many elements - but I did all of the art, design, and programming so it’s about 95% me.[/i]

[list]
[*] [b]What's the proudest feature/thing you've added or worked on in the game? Anything specific that gave you a lot of trouble? [/b]
[/list] [i]I’m most proud of the graphics-related effects I’ve added to the game, like GPU particle effects, weather effects, shaders, and compute shader stuff. I learned most of those things from scratch throughout development, so it was very exciting to figure these things out and then put them into the game. The thing that gave me a lot of trouble were controls and usability-related issues. These things take a lot of time and QA effort to resolve, so it’s been challenging to figure out.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] How long is the game? And also can we play after finishing the game?
[/list][/b] [i]It depends on the player’s skill, but I think it’ll be around 4-7 hours for most people. There are hidden secrets, game modes and you can challenge your timed records, so players can enjoy the game even after finishing the main story. [/i]

[b][list]
[*] Did COVID influence you or the development in any way?
[/list][/b] [i]Being a solo developer, I wasn’t impacted as greatly as bigger teams have been due to restrictions forcing people to work from home. However, all of the video game conferences and trade shows being canceled or switching to online was a big change, as I relied on player and developer feedback heavily in previous games I worked on. Also, the constant fear and uncertainty of the pandemic early on probably had an impact on my psyche.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] What do you think, if you had a team, how much would the development time be reduced, and what features would you be able to implement?
[/list][/b] [i]Making this exact game with a bigger team - maybe the development time could’ve been reduced by 30%. Games take some time to cook, so it’s really hard to estimate. [/i]

[b][list]
[*] What or who inspired or influenced you to make this game?
[/list][/b] [i]Many elements of Korean culture influenced me - old architecture, early 20th-century history, miniature models of old Korean cities at museums, Korean folklore, and horror, etc.[/i]
 
[b][list]
[*] Why was backstab abandoned in the final version? I saw in Devlogs that you originally conceived this feature.
[/list][/b] [i]This mechanic is still in the game, but you may have to do some work to find it.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] In your opinion, what is the best-modeled area in the game? 
[/list][/b] [i]I like the areas outside of the main missions. The graveyard has a comfy feeling for me, having spent so much time there. And there are other relaxing areas later on in the game that I really enjoy being in.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] Do you have time to play games, or do you prefer to take a break from development in other ways? If by others, then by what?
[/list][/b] [i]I play many games, sometimes to relax and other times to learn from other developers. Outside of games, I like to exercise, play music, or watch horror movies to take a break.[/i]

[b][list]
[*] In terms of replayability, how many different endings will there be/are there?
[/list][/b] [i]The main story has one ending, but there are many secrets and game modes for replayability.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37518397/152fb1419df0940f7b1106ba900a0a3f6c12c315.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Wonhon Introduction
notes.notes:
Welcome everyone to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1294340/Wonhon_A_Vengeful_Spirit/]Wonhon: A Vengeful Spirit[/url]

Are you a fan of stealth focused games, with a heavy dose of the supernatural included? Wonhon may just be the game for you.

Play as the spirit of a girl who was brutally murdered in a bloody war, but who has now returned from beyond the grave as a vengeful spirit and is looking for revenge. 

Inspired by Korean folklore and culture, you will be able to travel through an authentic representation of historical Korea while using your powers to dispose of your enemies.

We have been silently working on our game for a while now, but as progress has been excellent we are happy to finally join Steam and announce our tentative release date: December 2020.

We look forward to seeing our community grow and encourage you to join our discussions section to let us know what you think!
